skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest radiograph showing complete opacification (white-out) of a hemithorax to determine the underlying etiology.
steps: Assess the position of the mediastinal structures (trachea, heart border) relative to the side of the opacity.
If the mediastinum is shifted away from the opacity (contralateral shift), identify the cause as a space-occupying lesion exerting mass effect, such as a massive pleural effusion or large tumor.
If the mediastinum is shifted toward the opacity (ipsilateral shift), identify the cause as volume loss, such as total lung atelectasis or pneumonectomy.
If the mediastinum remains central, consider causes that do not significantly alter intrathoracic volume or pressure, such as extensive pneumonia.
